definition: The AsoSoft text corpus is the first large-scale Kurdish text corpus, collected and processed by the AsoSoft research and development group.
details: It contains 458,000 documents (188 million tokens) that are collected from sources such as websites, news agencies, books, and magazines. The corpus is partially tagged by topic, so it can be used for topic identification tasks. Also, it is applicable for extracting language model and computational lexicon information. Part of the corpus (75 million tokens) is available online for non-commercial use. The corpus uses the TEI format.

explainer.lead: The AsoSoft text corpus is a large collection of Kurdish writing assembled by the AsoSoft research and development group, and the first Kurdish corpus of this scale. Its 458,000 documents give researchers material for studying topics, language patterns and vocabulary rather than relying on very small text samples.

tiers.eli5: Think of it as a giant digital library of Kurdish writing, with pages gathered from websites, news reports, books and magazines. Researchers can use it to teach computers about Kurdish words and what different pieces of writing are about. Some of the library is also organised by topic, which makes those lessons easier.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers can parse the TEI-formatted documents to build Kurdish language models, derive computational lexicons, or experiment with topic identification using the partially tagged material. Account for the mixture of web, news, book and magazine text when designing experiments, and do not treat every document as topic-labelled. The online subset contains 75 million tokens and is available for non-commercial use.
tiers.paperLevel: The corpus is a TEI-encoded Kurdish document collection D with |D| = 458,000 documents and 188 million tokens, collected from websites, news agencies, books and magazines. Topic annotations cover only part of D, while an online subset contains 75 million tokens for non-commercial use; the resource supplies corpus data for language-model, computational-lexicon and topic-identification work, not an evaluation score.

explainer.example: The online subset contains 75 million of the corpus's 188 million tokens. Its share is 75 / 188 × 100 ≈ 39.9%, so roughly two fifths of the corpus's tokens are in that subset.

usedIn.name: Topic identification
usedIn.detail: The partially topic-tagged documents can support work on assigning subjects to Kurdish text.

usedIn.name: Kurdish language modelling
usedIn.detail: The corpus's 188 million tokens provide material for extracting language-model information.

usedIn.name: Computational lexicography
usedIn.detail: Its collected documents can be used to derive information for computational lexicons.

explainer.measures: It does not measure model performance or assign a quality score. It measures the scale of a Kurdish text resource through its document and token counts, while supplying text and partial topic annotations for language research.
howScored: Corpus size is reported as 458,000 documents.
The full collection contains 188 million tokens.
The online non-commercial subset contains 75 million tokens.
Topic coverage is partial rather than a score over every document.
explainer.formula: There is no scoring formula; corpus coverage can be summarised by document count, token count and the number of tokens in the available subset.
explainer.typicalResults: A typical output is a collection of TEI-encoded Kurdish texts, with topic tags on part of the collection. Downstream results can include topic-identification data, language-model statistics or computational-lexicon information.
caveats: Only part of the corpus is tagged by topic.
Its texts span several kinds of sources and writing.
The 75-million-token online subset is limited to non-commercial use.
The corpus is a resource, not a benchmark score.
